claim: The r806919 type dump names no SpiralDoor behavior class: the only door behavior classes are CastleBlockDoor and ObstacleCourseRevolvingDoor. The Spiral Door (template id 84113 in the reference) must therefore be a generic teleporter template whose mark lives in property values, not in class presence. It carries a TeleportProximityBehaviorTemplate (class hash 1330192380, 9 properties, all Save|Copy|Public) — the same behavior family 10.13 assigns to go-home and marked world teleporters — so a behavior-presence match alone cannot select the Spiral Door. The distinguishing property values on template 84113 are unverified and need a bindecode of that template from a real install.
confidence_notes: High for the negative result (no SpiralDoor class in the dump's class list) and for the reference mechanism (manifest id to archive/path to m_behaviors). Medium overall because the distinguishing property values on template 84113 itself are unverified without a client install.
disproof: A bindecode of template 84113 from the same client revision shows no TeleportProximityBehaviorTemplate among its m_behaviors; or the type dump names a dedicated SpiralDoor behavior class the vocabulary sweep missed; or a fresh vocabulary built from the same dump lists different hashes or property counts for the three teleport classes.
evidence: doc/roadmap/phase-10-play-the-wizard-city-opening-quests.md:823 records that the reference identifies the Spiral Door by hard-coded template id 84113 and that the identification is unverified; the line entered with 4046437.

A sweep of every class in contrib/findings/objects/type_property_flag_vocabulary.json finds no class whose name contains 'SpiralDoor'. The only door behavior classes are CastleBlockDoor (hash 46182351) / CastleBlockDoorBehaviorTemplate (hash 2140381725, 1 property) and ObstacleCourseRevolvingDoor (hash 296406079) / ObstacleCourseRevolvingDoorBehaviorTemplate (hash 914357476, 8 properties), neither of which is a world teleporter.

The same vocabulary names class TeleportProximityBehaviorTemplate (hash 1330192380) with 9 properties, every one flagged Save|Copy|Public, plus the runtime class TeleportProximityBehavior (hash 58611215) and TeleportProximityBehaviorBase (hash 327108655).

The 10.13 spec's own teleporter list is 'Spiral Door, go-home, marked world teleporters' (phase-10-play-the-wizard-city-opening-quests.md:792), all clicked objects; its deliverable is interact dispatch for objects whose template has teleport behaviors, with the Spiral Door answering MSG_WORLDTELEPORTLIST from world.world_hub rows gated by unlocked worlds.

doc/ARCHITECTURE.md (Object templates, settled 2026-09-25): TemplateManifest.xml in Root.wad maps each template id to its archive and path; a template decodes as a CoreTemplate-derived object; its behaviors live in m_behaviors and are named by m_behaviorName, which src/server/game/Entities/ObjectTemplateMgr.cpp:339 reads per behavior entry.

No client install or type dump exists on this machine, and object templates are decoded at run time from the user's own install and never committed (ARCHITECTURE.md, 'Bring your own files'), so template 84113's property values could not be read here.
how_to_repeat: Read Bin/revision.dat from your own client installation and confirm it identifies r806919.Wizard_1_610.
Run the project's client template command against that installation to find template 84113's manifest entry (archive and ObjectData path).
Run bindecode --compact on that entry with the installation's type dump and list its m_behaviors entries with their classes.
Record the TeleportProximityBehaviorTemplate instance's 9 property names and values (10.13 names m_radius, m_locationName and m_requirementList; record the remaining six from the dump).

Decode a go-home teleporter and a marked world teleporter template the same way and diff the three TeleportProximityBehaviorTemplate instances: the property values that select the Spiral Door, and only it, are the F-67 answer.
Re-run the class-name sweep over the type dump's class list to confirm no class named *SpiralDoor* exists.
match_rule_status: Behavior presence is necessary but not sufficient: 10.13 lists the Spiral Door alongside go-home and marked world teleporters as teleporter objects, so the server must match on distinguishing property values of the TeleportProximityBehaviorTemplate instance, not on the behavior's presence. Those values are the open item for a bindecode run against a real install.
subject: How the Spiral Door is marked in the object templates
